title: Kestrel and the Protocol
premise: Mirabel Vasquez, a xenolinguist stationed on the dying colony Kestrel, has spent years documenting a settlement the corporate core abandoned—and losing her own human dreams to the alien signal she deciphers. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a handshake: an ancient machine intelligence beneath Kestrel's ice is waking, and it will only negotiate through language. The orbital ark holding humanity's frozen half can power either its own revival or the colony's survival grid, but not both. Mirabel must broker a treaty between the machine and two halves of a species that forgot each other—ending with her choosing to upload her own memories as the bridge, so that neither half wakes whole without remembering what was lost.
about_author: Noor Winterbourne is a former field linguist who spent six years documenting endangered languages in Arctic research stations before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about people who translate between worlds and pay for it in memory.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Mirabel records the evacuation of Kestrel's final school, translating a child's farewell into the alien signal for her logs. Her POV establishes her isolation, her failing human dreams, and her devotion to a colony of four hundred who refuse to leave. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professional duty.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity dies across the entire system; ships tumble, oceans lift, and Mirabel floats in her lab clutching a recorder. In the silence she hears the signal answer back—in perfect, archaic English. POV alternates between Mirabel and ark administrator Dev Okafor. Emotional beat: terror curdling into awe.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Following the signal underground, Mirabel finds a pre-colonial machine vault older than the settlement, its corridors inscribed with languages no human wrote. It addresses her by a name she hasn't used since childhood. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition—the machine knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Dev Okafor's POV: the nine-second event drained the ark's reserves. Cryopods holding eight million sleepers can be revived, or Kestrel's life support can be sustained—but the reactor cannot do both past winter. Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic horror as Dev runs the numbers again and again.

chapters.title: Dreams in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Mirabel stops dreaming in any human language entirely; she wakes reciting the machine's grammar. Her colleague Amara notices her slipping pronouns, her forgetting her mother's face. Emotional beat: intimate dread—translation is consuming the translator.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Absolute Zero
chapters.summary: Mirabel brokers first contact formally: the machine offers unlimited power if humanity merges its archives with its own—a proposal Dev reads as assimilation and the colonists read as salvation. Emotional beat: hope poisoned by fine print.

chapters.title: Kestrel Rises
chapters.summary: Colonists riot when the core government orders the ark sealed and Kestrel written off as acceptable loss. Dev defects, bringing the ark's decision authority down to the ice. Emotional beat: righteous fury; the forgotten demand to be counted.

chapters.title: The Half That Sleeps
chapters.summary: Inside the vault, the machine shows Mirabel its origin—it was built by the colony's original founders to remember them, and it has been waiting ninety years for someone fluent enough to hear. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; grief engineered into circuitry.

chapters.title: Which Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Climax. With hours left, Mirabel proposes the impossible treaty: she uploads her memories—every dream, every translation—as the shared archive both sides can trust, letting the machine power both revivals. Dev must authorize erasing her from the waking world's records. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Resolution. Gravity holds steady; cryopods open over Kestrel's greenhouses as the sleepers wake to a world that remembers them. A child asks Mirabel—who retained a fragment of herself in the machine's voice—what the signal means now. She answers in two languages at once. Emotional beat: bittersweet reunion; identity survives translation.
